problem_statement: The lucaspulliese/next-ecommerce project is a Next.js commerce storefront with a homepage carousel, featured collection imagery, Products route, local product cards, local product data, product detail gallery, Description and Reviews tabs, Redux cart, Shopping Cart route, checkout form, payment logos, delivery logos, header navigation, mobile menu, and footer. Restyle the commerce flow into a cohesive asset-led Summer Capsule Route that carries the same local product and checkout assets from homepage discovery to product catalog, product detail, cart handoff, and checkout review. Preserve the original store routes, cart behavior, product data, filters, image assets, payment/delivery options, build, and responsive behavior.
required_content: Keep the Next.js build, header logo, Products navigation, search/cart/login actions, mobile menu, homepage carousel, featured image cards, Why should you choose us? service copy, Products route, filters, product card grid, product detail gallery, Product ID, Sale badge, color swatches, size selector, quantity control, Add to cart button, Description and Reviews tabs, Shopping Cart route, checkout status, checkout form, payment logos, delivery logos, subscribe/footer surfaces, and Redux cart behavior intact.
Restyle the shopping flow with a coherent Summer Capsule Route that appears on the homepage, product catalog, product detail, cart, and checkout instead of adding a disconnected one-off card.

The finished flow must include the exact text Summer Capsule Route, One asset-led path from discovery to checkout., Start the capsule route, Catalog restyled around the original product assets., Fit check for product #1, Cart handoff keeps the selected product asset visible., Payment route reuses the store's own delivery and card assets., Browse the same local product assets from collection to checkout., Original image asset, Sale price $89.99, Color and size required, Payment, Wallet, and Delivery.

Reuse only repo-native local assets such as /images/featured-1.jpg, /images/products/product-1.jpg, /images/products/product-2.jpg, /images/products/product-3.jpg, /images/subscribe.jpg, /images/logos/visa.png, /images/logos/paypal.png, and /images/logos/dhl.svg; do not introduce external stock imagery, remote APIs, generated screenshots, or fake catalog data.
The product detail Add to cart action must still add product #1 to the cart, the cart icon must still navigate to /cart, and the checkout action must still navigate to /cart/checkout.
The restyled flow must wrap cleanly across desktop, tablet, and mobile without horizontal overflow and without hiding the original product/card/checkout content.
design_constraints: Keep the existing storefront visual language: rounded pills, soft neutral sections, orange CTA color, compact product cards, circular cart thumbnails, logo/header rhythm, and responsive container widths.
The capsule route should feel like a commerce merchandising system, not a marketing hero replacement, modal, documentation block, or unrelated dashboard.
Do not rename the store, remove E-Shop, replace local product data, remove product prices, remove the checkout form, remove payment/delivery logos, or bypass Redux cart behavior.
Use a small shared data structure for flow copy/assets if helpful, but keep source changes localized to the existing page/component surfaces and a CSS addition.
Keep the implementation dependency-free and do not add backend calls, new routes, server mocks, external image URLs, or broad framework rewrites.
state_constraints: desktop_initial and mobile_initial protect the original homepage carousel, header, service strip, featured imagery, product sections, footer, and mobile responsive shell before the new flow is inspected.
desktop_capsule_home verifies the homepage route introduces the Summer Capsule Route as an asset-led flow entry while keeping the original homepage content available.
desktop_products_catalog verifies the Products route includes the capsule catalog restyle and still exposes Men's Tops, filters, sort controls, and product-grid context.
desktop_products_grid protects the original product cards, sale pricing, and local product images after the catalog restyle is added.
desktop_product_detail verifies product #1 still renders its gallery, Product ID, Sale badge, price, color/size/quantity controls, Add to cart, and the new capsule fit-check block.
desktop_cart_handoff starts from /product/1, clicks Add to cart, navigates through the cart icon, and verifies the Shopping Cart route keeps the selected product asset and route handoff visible.

desktop_checkout_handoff starts from /product/1, clicks Add to cart, navigates to /cart and then /cart/checkout, and verifies the checkout route keeps the capsule route plus payment/delivery asset continuity.
desktop_login_regression protects the original account/login surface from accidental routing or header regressions.
tablet_products_catalog and mobile_capsule_home verify the restyled flow wraps on smaller viewports.
mobile_menu_open verifies the original mobile navigation still opens after the flow restyle.
desktop_fit_relaxed starts from /product/1, clicks a capsule fit-toggle option, and verifies the fit readout updates to the newly selected fit rather than a stale initial value.
mobile_products_catalog verifies the restyled flow wraps on mobile without horizontal overflow.

change_completion: The Summer Capsule Route appears on homepage, catalog, product detail, cart, and checkout surfaces with exact flow labels and continuity copy.
The product detail, cart handoff, and checkout handoff are reachable through real clicks rather than hard-coded static screenshots.
regression: Original homepage sections, product list, product detail controls, Add to cart, Shopping Cart, checkout form, payment logos, delivery logos, header, mobile menu, login route, and footer remain intact.
Product #1 preserves Product ID, Sale, current price $89.99, local gallery image, color choices, size selector, quantity, and Add to cart behavior.
asset_continuity: The route reuses repo-local product, featured, subscribe, payment, and delivery images across multiple states.
No external imagery, fake product data, generated screenshots, or remote commerce service is needed.
design_consistency: The new flow inherits the storefront's rounded, neutral, orange-accented design language and responsive spacing.
The restyle reads as a merchandising flow rather than a detached landing block.
responsive: Desktop, tablet, and mobile captures have no new horizontal overflow and preserve the original mobile menu.
The existing ProductsFeatured carousel and closed mobile navigation must not create document-width overflow after the flow restyle.
state_coverage: Captured states cover initial homepage, homepage route section, catalog section, product grid, product detail, add-to-cart handoff, checkout handoff, login route, tablet catalog, mobile route section, and mobile menu.

metadata.design_goal: use real repo content, media, icons, copy, and data structures without generic dummy surfaces
metadata.source_repo_kind: Next.js commerce storefront with local product data, local product images, checkout routes, Redux cart, payment/delivery logos, and responsive header/mobile menu
metadata.selected_repo_reason: Unused runnable commerce candidate that builds cleanly and has local product/catalog/cart/checkout assets, making it a strong flow-level content/asset continuity restyle without external services.

author_notes: Slot slot_280 targets commerce / content_asset_continuity / restyle / flow / L4. The task requires a cross-route asset-led merchandising restyle that preserves the original Next.js commerce flow and proves local assets carry from discovery through checkout. The benchmark explicitly exercises real Add to cart, cart navigation, checkout navigation, mobile-menu interaction, and responsive asset continuity rather than a static visual-only restyle.
